decoded.what-it-establishes: the endpoint answers a syntactically valid JSON document that is not a JSON-RPC request with HTTP 200 and the JSON-RPC code -32700, "Parse error". The payload sent was {}, which parses. Under the JSON-RPC 2.0 specification -32700 is for "Invalid JSON was received by the server" and -32600, Invalid Request, is for "The JSON sent is not a valid Request object", which is what {} is. So the code names the wrong fault, and a client that distinguishes a transport-level parse failure from a malformed request will read this as the former. The status is 200, which is this endpoint's established habit: three refusals delivered inside 200s are already recorded in this pull request.

A request missing jsonrpc and method is the only shape measured here, and nothing is claimed about a well-formed request with a bad member, which was not sent. It also establishes nothing about the rate limit: the six requests were spaced 10 to 11 seconds apart, which is denser than the 25-second spacing of this pull request's tools/call records and was chosen because the question here is whether one request shape answers consistently. No 429 was drawn at this spacing; that is not a measurement of the limit, which stays unmeasured (p-20260930-aws-knowledge-mcp-anonymous-429).

Two of the three with the header answered 200 and one answered 500; all three without it answered 200. The header does not separate the two outcomes, and with three readings per arm nothing stronger than that is claimed.

finding: The AWS Knowledge MCP endpoint answers a keyless POST of the document {} with HTTP 200 and the JSON-RPC error code -32700, "Parse error - Invalid JSON format". The document it calls invalid JSON is valid JSON. Under the JSON-RPC 2.0 specification the code for a parsed document that is not a Request object is -32600, Invalid Request; -32700 is reserved for text the server could not parse. Five of six identical requests sent between 06:11Z and 06:12Z on 2026-10-01 answered exactly this, 94 bytes each; the sixth answered HTTP 500 and is recorded separately. This is the request the registry's own link gate sends to this surface, so the two records together are why that gate passes and fails on the same head.
